doc.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20

title: First job with the Olympia band
summary: He took Elmore Chalvin's place in his first band, stayed a couple of years, and began brass band work before the Depression.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: A drummer by the name of the bass and all the bass. No drumming.

How many trumpets did they have at that time? Well, I was the only one I worked with. I know I was a tiny band because I was split up like that. Take me in, you know. Oh, I see. Like my plans. Whose place did you take? A fellow by the name of Cuckoo. It's called Cuckoo. Oh, Elmore Chalvin. Brother-in-law. Yeah, I'm a tower, I'm a tower. Oh, yeah. He's brother-in-law. Brother-in-law, yeah. To Deep Pass. And I take my place. Oh, I see. Oh, yeah. I have one.
And how long did you stay with the bass?

A couple of years. A couple of years. He's got a lot of work. I'm getting all those eternity dance. And I like my plan. He's taking me on the wing in the West Meek. Oh, I see. With the ropes, you know. Beginning.
Well, did you play any brass band jobs at that time? No, not at that time. Only afterwards. When did you start playing with the brass bands? A year. Before depression hit?
Oh, yeah, yeah. Before the depression. Before the depression.
